crusadecraft.cb.conquest.desc: Take a province by force of arms alone. Victory: the province is yours. Costs prestige to declare.
crusadecraft.cb.vassalize.desc: Force a lower-ranked realm to swear fealty. Victory: it becomes your vassal (25% tax, 25% levies).
crusadecraft.cb.humiliate.desc: Avenge an insult. Victory: your enemy pays you a quarter of their treasury and loses prestige.
crusadecraft.war.cb.no_claim: No claim on their provinces: seal one at the Chancery Table first.
crusadecraft.war.cb.need_kingdom: Only a kingdom can press a de jure right.

crusadecraft.war.cb.need_duchy: You must be at least a duke to wage a war of conquest.
crusadecraft.war.cb.no_prestige: Not enough prestige to justify a conquest.
crusadecraft.war.cb.already_vassal: This realm already swears fealty to another liege.

crusadecraft.war.cb.no_rivalry: No insult to avenge: you need an open rivalry, or an opinion of −20 or lower.

crusadecraft.war.cb.none: No casus belli against this realm.

crusadecraft.war.block.liege: You cannot wage war on your liege or your vassal.

crusadecraft.war.block.alliance: You are allies: break the alliance at the Dovecote first.
crusadecraft.war.block.non_aggression: A non-aggression pact binds you: break it at the Dovecote first.
crusadecraft.war.peace.white.desc: Everyone goes home; nobody gains anything. A truce follows.
crusadecraft.war.peace.victory.desc: Your enemy concedes: your war goal is granted, or they pay reparations if they attacked you.
crusadecraft.war.peace.surrender.desc: You concede, at once and under your seal. Your enemy gets what they demanded.
crusadecraft.war.peace.to_player: A letter will go to the other ruler, who will decide for themselves.

crusadecraft.war.map.tip: Open the war map: your battle plan, your allies' plans, the front line and the sieges under way.
crusadecraft.war.nobody: No known realm. Send your heralds, or travel the world: the realms you discover appear here.
crusadecraft.war.strength.compare.tip: Their estimated strength against yours. An army at rest only counts for a third: raise it before going on campaign.
crusadecraft.war.declare.tip: Your allies and vassals will follow you; so will theirs. First click arms, second click declares.
crusadecraft.war.score.title: War score
crusadecraft.war.score.desc:
Right of the centre, your side has the upper hand.
It rises with battles won (skirmishes, sieges, raids repelled),
occupied provinces, and every day spent holding the target province.
The higher it is, the likelier your enemy accepts your terms.
crusadecraft.war.allies.count: Allies: %s on your side, %s on theirs
crusadecraft.war.journal.empty: Nothing yet: the armies are looking for each other.
crusadecraft.war.not_leader: Only the ruler leading their side can negotiate peace.
crusadecraft.war.tab.hint: Raise the army, declare and negotiate: at the War Table.
crusadecraft.war.army.title: The realm's army
crusadecraft.war.army.desc: Six men per guard in your colonies, and one per three citizens. Raised, it counts in full but costs one gold coin per ten men per day; at rest, it replenishes.
crusadecraft.war.army.raise.tip: The whole army takes the field, and your men-at-arms follow you to sieges. Pay: %s coins a day.
crusadecraft.war.army.disband.tip: The men go home: no more pay, but the army only counts for a third.
crusadecraft.war.army.raised: The army is raised: %s men on campaign.
crusadecraft.war.army.disbanded: The army is sent home (%s men).
crusadecraft.war.antigrief: In enemy territory, walls only fall to explosives, and rise again at peace.
crusadecraft.toast.war.declared.title: War is declared

crusadecraft.toast.war.called.title: Call to arms
crusadecraft.toast.war.called.body: %s calls you to their side against %s.
crusadecraft.toast.war.skirmish.title: Skirmish
crusadecraft.toast.war.peace.title: Peace is signed
crusadecraft.toast.war.siege.title: Siege of %s
crusadecraft.toast.war.siege.body: The garrison sallies out: %s soldiers. Hold the banner to take the place.
crusadecraft.toast.war.siege_lifted.body: You moved away: the garrison returns to its walls.
crusadecraft.toast.war.captured.title: Stronghold taken!
crusadecraft.toast.war.captured.body: The banner of %s has fallen: %s raises its own.
crusadecraft.toast.war.raid.title: Enemy raid!
crusadecraft.toast.war.raid_lost.title: Raid: plundered!
crusadecraft.letter.peace_surrender.body: Arms have decided against us. By this letter, %s lays down its arms and accepts your terms. Seal it, and peace will be made to your advantage.
crusadecraft.letter.peace_demand.subject: Summons
crusadecraft.letter.peace_demand.body: The fortunes of war have spoken. By this letter, %s demands your surrender. Seal it, and peace will be made on our terms; refuse, and the war goes on.
crusadecraft.letter.peace_accept.subject: Your peace is accepted
crusadecraft.letter.peace_accept.body: By this letter, %s accepts your terms: %s. Seal it, and the war will end.
crusadecraft.letter.peace_refuse.subject: Your peace offer is rejected
crusadecraft.letter.peace_refuse.body: Your terms are rejected: %s will fight on.
crusadecraft.letter.peace_player.subject: An offer of peace
crusadecraft.letter.peace_player.body: %s offers you peace on these terms: %s (from their side). Seal this letter to accept.
crusadecraft.news.title: News of the world
crusadecraft.toast.news.title: News of the world
crusadecraft.toast.coalition.title: A coalition forms!
crusadecraft.toast.coalition.body: %s realms band together against you: your expansion worries them.
crusadecraft.toast.coalition_end.title: Coalition dissolved
crusadecraft.toast.coalition_end.body: Your neighbours feel safer: the coalition against you breaks up.
crusadecraft.toast.war.occupied.title: Stronghold occupied
crusadecraft.letter.ai_war.subject: Declaration of war
crusadecraft.letter.ai_war.body: By this letter, %s declares war on you. Casus belli: %s. Look to your defences: our armies are on the march.
crusadecraft.letter.peace_white.subject: An offer of white peace
crusadecraft.letter.peace_white.body: This war has lasted long enough. By this letter, %s proposes that everyone goes home, giving nothing up. Seal it, and peace will be made.
crusadecraft.war.threat.title: Threat
crusadecraft.war.threat.desc:
Your conquests and wars worry your neighbours, and their opinion suffers for it.
Each conquered province adds 20, each declaration of war 5; it falls back every day.
Above %s, those who fear you band together in a coalition.
crusadecraft.toast.event.body: A decision awaits you (%s day(s)): realm menu, K key.
crusadecraft.event.fx.subject: Character's opinion: %s
crusadecraft.event.default: Applies by default if you do not decide.
crusadecraft.event.gone: This matter no longer awaits an answer.
crusadecraft.event.famine.title: Famine
crusadecraft.event.famine.text: The granaries ring hollow. In the colonies bread is rationed and people grumble against the crown: the mayors want the treasury to buy grain.
crusadecraft.event.peste.title: The fever
crusadecraft.event.peste.text: A malignant fever spreads from house to house. Healers speak of closing the gates and burning the straw beds; meanwhile soldiers fall ill in the barracks.
crusadecraft.event.peste.opt.chaplain: Entrust the sick to the chaplain
crusadecraft.event.prosperite.title: Happy days
crusadecraft.event.prosperite.text: The people are content, the markets overflow and there is singing in the squares at night. Your councillors suggest marking the occasion — or making the most of it.
crusadecraft.event.prosperite.opt.feast: Throw a feast for the people
crusadecraft.event.prosperite.opt.church: Make an offering to the Church
Your chancellor comes to the audience: he asks to sign certain letters alone, "to save time". His rivals see a hand reaching for the seal.
crusadecraft.event.duel.title: A challenge
crusadecraft.event.duel.text: A knight-errant throws down his gauntlet before your marshal and challenges the valour of your arms in front of the whole court.
crusadecraft.event.duel.opt.accept: Let the marshal take up the challenge
crusadecraft.event.duel.opt.refuse: Have the insolent man thrown out
crusadecraft.event.festin.title: Time for a feast
crusadecraft.event.festin.text: The season is right and the court is bored. A great feast would be talked about to the borders — and empty the treasury.
crusadecraft.event.chasse.title: A hunting party
crusadecraft.event.chasse.text: The huntsmen have flushed a great stag in the woods of the demesne. Your councillors wait to know whether you will join the hunt.
crusadecraft.event.pelerins.title: Pilgrims
crusadecraft.event.pelerins.text: A band of pilgrims asks for shelter and passage. They are poor, pious and numerous; the steward points out that they cross your tolls.
crusadecraft.event.marchand.title: A merchant from overseas
crusadecraft.event.marchand.text: A merchant from afar offers silks, spices and a silver astrolabe. He is also looking for a partner in the realm.
crusadecraft.event.brigands.title: Brigands on the roads
crusadecraft.event.brigands.text: Brigands are holding travellers to ransom between your colonies. The mayors want action before the merchants desert the roads.
crusadecraft.event.brigands.opt.ignore: The roads are the mayors' business
crusadecraft.event.recolte.title: A fine harvest
crusadecraft.event.recolte.text: The harvest has been generous. Sheaves pile up and the peasants hope for a harvest festival.
crusadecraft.event.predicateur.title: A preacher
crusadecraft.event.predicateur.text: A barefoot preacher harangues the crowds: he denounces the luxury of the mighty and the tithes. The people listen; the clergy worry.
crusadecraft.event.predicateur.opt.expel: Drive him out of the realm
crusadecraft.event.ralliement.title: The call to arms
crusadecraft.event.ralliement.text: The war drags on. Your captains propose raising new companies: volunteers for gold, or else a forced levy.
crusadecraft.event.heritier.title: The question of an heir
crusadecraft.event.heritier.text: The years pass and the court wonders: who will wear the crown after you? Proclaiming an heir would reassure your vassals.
crusadecraft.event.faction_baisse_impots: Led by %1$s, a court faction demands lower taxes. Its members no longer hide their anger: refuse, and the colonies will stop paying.
%2$s wants to leave the realm. %1$s speaks in its name: the province will govern itself, or rise up.
crusadecraft.event.faction_changement.te: Led by %1$s, a faction demands the dismissal of %2$s, whom it blames for every ill in the realm.
crusadecraft.event.plot_discovered.title: A plot uncovered
crusadecraft.event.plot_discovered.text: Your spymaster has proof: %1$s was preparing a %2$s. The culprit does not yet know you know.
crusadecraft.event.plot_succeeded.title: A plot has succeeded
crusadecraft.event.plot_succeeded.text: The blow has fallen, and nobody saw it coming until afterwards: %1$s was behind this %2$s.
crusadecraft.event.revolt.title: The peasants rise up
crusadecraft.event.revolt.text: In %2$s, hungry and overtaxed peasants have driven out the tax collectors. They will pay nothing more until they are heard.
crusadecraft.event.revolt.opt.wait: Wait for the anger to fade
crusadecraft.faction.baisse_impots.desc: Its members want taxes lowered one step.
crusadecraft.faction.independance.desc: An unhappy province wants to leave the realm.
crusadecraft.faction.changement.desc: Its members want to drive out a councillor they hate.

crusadecraft.intrigue.no_spy: Without a spymaster, you know nothing of what is afoot.
crusadecraft.intrigue.dread.tip: The dread you inspire weakens factions (by half its value).
crusadecraft.intrigue.rumours: Whispers are going round: %s faction(s) forming in the shadows.

crusadecraft.intrigue.secrets.unknown: Without a spymaster, secrets stay well kept.
crusadecraft.intrigue.blackmail.tip: They will keep quiet for two months — no faction, no plot — but will not forget. Dread +3.
crusadecraft.intrigue.expose.tip: Justice is done in plain sight: prestige +5, but they will hold it against you for a long time.
crusadecraft.intrigue.open.tip: Factions, plots and secrets uncovered by your spymaster.
crusadecraft.toast.faction.title: A faction is forming

crusadecraft.chronicles.no_realm: A realm is needed for its chronicles to be written.

crusadecraft.war.cb.no_piety: Not enough piety: a crusade costs 100.

crusadecraft.codex.name: CrusadeCraft Codex
crusadecraft.codex.subtitle: Ruling a realm
crusadecraft.codex.landing: Your MineColonies colonies become a realm: a council of real citizens, a treasury, laws, neighbours to win over or subdue, wars, intrigues and a court.$(br2)Each chapter explains one part of the game, in the order you discover it.
crusadecraft.codex.cat.guerre.desc: Casus belli, armies, sieges, peace, crusades.
crusadecraft.codex.fondation.p0: Place the $(l)Royal Throne$() in the Town Hall of a colony you own (level 2 or more), then right-click it: pick a name, a motto, a house and colours. The colony becomes your capital.
crusadecraft.codex.fondation.p1: The $(k:key.crusadecraft.realm_menu) key (K by default) opens the realm menu: realm, council, vassals, diplomacy, treasury, war, laws, chronicles. The $(l)Register$() shows your colonies; a button on the Town Hall window also opens the menu.
crusadecraft.codex.conseil.p0: Your councillors are real citizens. With the $(l)Sceptre$(), right-click a citizen: their sheet, traits, stats (from their MineColonies skills) and opinion of you. Appoint them chancellor, marshal, steward, spymaster or chaplain.
crusadecraft.codex.conseil.p1: The $(l)Council Table$() gathers the council; each member gets a task (manage the demesne, train troops, hunt plots…). Mayors run each province from their $(l)Desk$(). The discontent bring requests, or band together.
crusadecraft.codex.tresor.p0: Every world day, colonies pay taxes according to their buildings and happiness; demesne income, wages and upkeep follow. The $(l)Treasury Chest$() takes and gives gold (nuggets, ingots, blocks).
crusadecraft.codex.tresor.p1: Laws (taxation, authority, chivalry, justice) are voted by the council, or forced through at a prestige cost. Some need University research.
crusadecraft.codex.carte.p0: AI realms live around you, set on real villages: you discover them by travelling, or by receiving their heralds. Nine $(l)War Table$() frames make a map; the "Map" button opens the world map, political or de jure.
crusadecraft.codex.diplomatie.p0: At the $(l)Dovecote$(), write to other rulers: treaties, gifts, insults, tributes, vassalage. Their answer can be read in advance, and comes by letter. An accepted letter is sealed with the $(l)Royal Seal$().
crusadecraft.codex.diplomatie.p1: The $(l)Chancery Table$() creates your titles (County, Duchy, Kingdom, Empire) once you have enough provinces, sets your vassals' contracts and has your chancellor fabricate claims.
crusadecraft.codex.guerre.p0: At the War Table, pick a realm and a casus belli: claim, de jure right, conquest, subjugation, humiliation. Your allies and vassals follow. Raise the army: it counts in full but costs pay.
crusadecraft.codex.guerre.p1: Each day, a skirmish. Approach the enemy capital: its garrison sallies out; hold its banner to take the place. The enemy raids your colonies. In enemy territory, only explosives break blocks, and everything is repaired at peace.
crusadecraft.codex.guerre.p2: Peace is negotiated at the Table: white peace, demand victory, surrender. Victory gives the target province, a vassal or gold. Mind your $(l)threat$(): too many conquests, and a coalition forms against you.
crusadecraft.codex.croisades.p0: Some realms are pagan or heretic. As at least a count, with 100 piety, declare a $(l)holy war$() on them: faithful realms rally, other rulers are called. Victory: the target province, and piety and prestige for every crusader.
crusadecraft.codex.evenements.p0: Famine, fever, feasts, pilgrims, brigands… An event awaits your decision for a few days ("Events" button of the realm menu); without an answer, the default option applies. Events are JSON files: a datapack can add more.
crusadecraft.codex.complots.p0: Discontent courtiers band into factions (lower taxes, independence, dismissal of a councillor) and issue ultimatums. Those who hate you plot. Your spymaster uncovers them, along with secrets good for blackmail.
crusadecraft.codex.complots.p1: All of this is shown in the $(l)Intrigues$() screen (Council tab). Dread, a marshal keeping order and a named heir weaken factions. Unhappy, overtaxed colonies revolt.
crusadecraft.codex.chroniques.p0: The chronicle of your reign writes itself: founding, titles, wars, conquests, laws, decisions. Read it in the Chronicles tab, along with world news, or in the $(l)Chronicles of the Realm$() book.
crusadecraft.codex.tournois.p0: Place $(l)Tournament Lists$() in your realm ("Chivalry" research). Your councillors and mayors joust against neighbouring champions: prestige for the host, a champion trait for the winner, sometimes wounds.
crusadecraft.codex.maison.p0: From the Realm tab, "House" button: bring citizens into your dynasty. Their spouses and children (the real MineColonies genealogy) follow. Name an heir to reassure the court.
crusadecraft.codex.maison.p1: Marry a free member into the family of an AI ruler of your faith: the answer can be read in advance, the letter is sealed, and both houses become allies.

crusadecraft.codex.bornage.p0: The $(l)Boundary staff$() (two sticks, a string, a red dye) draws borders on the ground. Right-click in the air for its menu: which realm, how to draw, and what to build.$(li)$(l)Polygon$(): corners on the ground, then a click near the first.$(li)$(l)Rectangle$(): two opposite corners.$(li)$(l)Walking$(): every cell you cross is painted.
crusadecraft.codex.bornage.p1: The outline shows as coloured dust before it is confirmed. $(l)Ctrl+Z$() undoes the last one and refunds the gold. In survival you only draw for your own realm, near your lands, and each cell costs gold. A cell held by another realm cannot be taken with the staff: that is a matter for war.
crusadecraft.codex.bornage.p2: The $(l)Build$() mode places a construction where you click, its entrance facing you: waymark, watchtower, camp, outpost, fort, and in the editor a keep or a peopled village. In survival it rises block by block. Once finished it holds the land around it, and an enemy can besiege it. A paper map also shows the realms' lands.

Each place has its $(l)sheet$(): who holds it, what it comes under, its population, and the text you write in it.

crusadecraft.codex.cartedeguerre.p1: Only the ruler draws the plan; their allies, suzerain and vassals see it on their own map, and they see theirs. The state of the war draws itself: the front line in red, occupied provinces striped in the occupier's colour, sieges under way with their garrison.$(br2)On Dynmap, the $(l)War map$() layer shows the plan to anyone who has the web map address.
crusadecraft.codex.cartereelle: A map of the real world
crusadecraft.codex.cartereelle.p0: The realm map shows the real landscape: seas, mountains, forests, deserts, shaded relief. Where you have been, these are the real surface colours; elsewhere, an $(l)estimate$() drawn from the world generator, without buildings or structures.$(br2)The view button goes from $(l)political$() to $(l)de jure$() then $(l)terrain$(), the landscape alone.
crusadecraft.codex.cartereelle.p1: The landscape is prepared on the side, without slowing the game: it arrives piece by piece, coarse first then fine, around what you are looking at. The wheel zooms smoothly.$(br2)The Nether has no terrain map: its rock ceiling hides everything.
